Subject: POC / Trial planning: workload intake & success criteria (Acme Health)

Hi Tom

really appreciated the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps so we're all aligned for a successful POC.

Recap (from our call)
- Primary goal: validate Redwood inference cost and latency on your internal triage model for clinical summarization.
- Target success criteria you flagged: p95 latency under ~200ms for typical queries, end-to-end quality parity with existing baseline, and predictable unit cost that fits your procurement thresholds.

We need a short workload intake so we can size the trial and provision the right flavors (hosted vs. dedicated). Can you confirm the following for the POC workload? If you don't have exact numbers, ballpark estimates are fine.

Workload / Traffic profile
- Typical RPS (requests per second):
- Peak RPS / burst behavior (short spikes):
- Average token length per request (input + expected output):
- Max token length expected (worst-case):
- Typical concurrency (simultaneous requests):
- Burst concurrency during peak / batch windows: 
- Any special patterns (daily windows, EMR-driven bursts at 02:00, batched jobs, long-running sessions):

Proposed POC plan (high level)
- 4-week trial: week 0 onboarding/kickoff, week 1 functional tests + perf baseline, week 2 scale tests (RPS/bursts), week 3 evaluation & handover.
- Deliverables: evaluation report, cost model, runbook for production cutover.
- Owners: Marissa (Redwood) will coordinate setup; Ben will handle infra/config and dedicated sizing; Tom / Acme engineering will provide dataset slice and test harness.

Attachments: I'm attaching a short POC-plan and an MVP evaluation checklist to make the intake easier (POC-plan.pdf, MVP-eval-checklist.xlsx).

Can you reply with the workload numbers and confirm whether a 4-week timeline works for you? If so, we'll propose kickoff next Tuesday (2027-03-29) and send a meeting invite.

Thanks
Marissa

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: POC / Trial planning: workload intake & success criteria (Acme Health)

Hi Marissa
thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers we discussed and adding a few details. We looked at the production traces to extract realistic numbers:

Workload / Traffic profile (Acme Health triage model)
- Typical RPS: 20 req/s (steady daytime traffic)
- Peak RPS: 150 req/s for short bursts (1-5 minutes) during morning triage windows
- Burst/incident spikes: up to 300 req/s for very short windows (30-90s) when a feed replays
- Average token length: ~120 tokens (input + output combined)
- 95th percentile token length: ~420 tokens
- Max token length observed: ~600 tokens (some long discharge summaries)
- Typical concurrency: 8 concurrent sessions across the service
- Burst concurrency: up to 40 concurrent during peak replay windows
- Special patterns: nightly batch ingestion from Claims at 02:00 for which we run larger batched inference jobs (~10k records over 30 minutes)

POC timeline: 4 weeks sounds right. Success criteria we care most about:
- p95 latency < 200ms for typical queries (120 tokens) under steady load
- Cost-per-1M tokens estimate for steady-state and peak scenarios
- No data leakage; audit logging must be available for all calls

I’ve attached our security questionnaire (Acme_Security_QA.docx)

we’ll start that in parallel. We can kickoff 2027-03-29. Please put Ben on invites for infra configuration.

Tom

Thanks Tom
this is super helpful. Pasting your numbers into the intake and flagging a few follow-ups so we can size properly.

Follow-ups / clarifications
- For the nightly batch (10k records over 30 minutes) do you expect low per-item token counts (e.g., <100) or will those jobs hit the 420-600 token range?
- For burst spikes (300 req/s), is the traffic short-lived (single-minute retries) or could it sustain for several minutes repeatedly?
- Do you have a test harness / replay script we can use to reproduce the burst behavior (preferred) or should Redwood produce a synthetic runner?

Immediate plan from Redwood side
- Ben will estimate dedicated sizing and provide a hosted-equivalent config for comparison. He'll propose instance types + estimated cost for the 4-week POC and a projection for production.
- I’ll create the perf plan and test matrix (steady-state, 1-min bursts, replay batch) and share a runbook by Friday.
- We’ll enable audit logging for all calls during the trial and provide a link to the logs.

Next steps / owners
- Marissa: finalize perf plan & send runbook (action: by 2027-03-26)
- Ben: sizing + cost estimate + infra checklist (action: by 2027-03-26)
- Tom: provide test harness or sample traces, and return security QA answers (action: by 2027-03-26)
- All: kickoff 2027-03-29 (tentative)

Ben





can you confirm you’re good to estimate for both hosted and dedicated? I’ll loop engineering if needed.

Thanks all,
Marissa
